runHint: This is a React + TypeScript + Vite Toss mini-app, NOT Unity. To drive the real build: cd to appDir, `npm install` if node_modules is missing, then `npm run dev` (the script is `granite dev`) and read the served URL from its output — do not assume a port. Drive it with Playwright (`npx playwright`, v1.62.1 is cached; it is NOT a project dependency, so do not expect `require('playwright')` from the project to resolve). Use a mobile context: viewport 390x844, hasTouch: true, isMobile: true. For two-finger gestures (pinch/pan) Playwright's touchscreen API only does taps — use CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` with two touchPoints, moved in 10-15 incremental steps. Also sweep 320/360/430px widths for Korean-text layout defects (a 390-only check has missed real clipping bugs on this project before). KNOWN NON-DEFECT: two identical TDS provider console errors appear on every load, doubled by React StrictMode — they are an artifact of dev-serving a Toss mini-app in a plain browser with no native Toss host, not an app bug; do not deduct for them. KILL DISCIPLINE: kill only the dev-server PID you started (`Stop-Process -Id <pid>`), never by image name (`taskkill /IM node.exe`) — other teams' servers and the HQ Telegram bridge run on this machine.
brief: Turn real spending/saving habits into a growing town — a Fortune-City-style gamified 가계부 (household ledger) rebuilt for Toss users. Director's verbatim brief (2026-08-02): "이 프로젝트의 목표는 포춘시티 앱을 토스에 맞게 변경하여 토스 사용자들을 위한 가계부 앱을 만드는거야." The reference mechanic is Fortune City: tracked spending/saving rewards the player with city-building progress. This is a mechanic to adapt, not a UI to skin.
targetPlayer: Toss app users who want budgeting to feel less like a chore — casual, "watch something grow" motivation (the same psychological hook as Fortune City / Forest), inside an app they already use daily for money. Score fun from THIS person's view, not an adult reviewer's.
flows: Drive all of these against the real build: (1) first-run onboarding (S1) — a brand-new user with no data; (2) manual ledger entry -> a building is founded, with amount-proportional building EXP (a large entry must visibly found a higher-level building than a tiny one — this was Gate-3 finding #1); (3) building level growth, Lv.N badge, and the non-blocking auto-dismiss tier-celebration banner (must NOT block the FAB or the entry sheet while it shows — this was finding #5); (4) F16 month-end settlement and the engraved YYYY-MM monument tile (director-approved must-keep feature); (5) building move — one-finger long-press drag to relocate; (6) pinch zoom + two-finger pan + the 전체 보기 toggle (ADDENDUM-09, just landed); (7) the 20x20 map with park/lake terrain and 1x1/1x2/2x1/2x2 multi-tile buildings; (8) abuse/edge passes: empty data, mashing, mid-action interruption, reload/resume. NOTE the cash-charge (캐시충전) path is a deliberate STUB — a successful purchase must be impossible until Toss payments are integrated. Reaching a success state there is a defect; the stub itself is not.

experts.name: 게임 디자이너
experts.catches: Does the loop close? Is the reward on time? Is it trivially exploitable? Is the amount-proportional EXP curve sane, or can a user trivially found max-level buildings?

experts.name: UX 리서처
experts.catches: Understandable without a tutorial? Where do players drop out? Does onboarding (S1) actually teach the loop, or just show text?

experts.name: 라이브옵스 PD
experts.catches: Is there a reason to open it tomorrow? Does progress feel owned? Do the monthly settlement and monuments create a return hook?

experts.name: QA 리드
experts.catches: Mashing, empty data, interruption, resume — does it hold? Do gestures collide (long-press vs pinch)? Does state survive reload?

experts.name: 타깃 플레이어
experts.catches: Would a real Toss user who finds budgeting a chore enjoy this, or only an adult reviewer? Is entering an expense worth the friction?

rubric.name: Core loop works end to end
